docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Welcome to the Gero documentation! This guide helps you get started with your own personal media platform.

docs.title: What is Gero?
docs.text:
Gero is a personal video content management and streaming platform. It lets you download, organize, tag, and enjoy your media collection through a modern web interface.

Install it on your Windows PC. All data stays on your own hardware — no cloud storage, no tracking, no analytics. See the Privacy policy for the one request Gero makes, and only when you ask it to.

docs.title: What you'll find here
docs.text: Section Description Installation How to get, install and update Gero on Windows Videos Importing, processing, and managing your video library Tags Automatic and manual content categorization Media subscriptions Auto-download from your favorite sources Arcade: Follow the Beat Auto-build a beat-synced video from your library, matched to the music Arcade: Caption Creator Multi-clip stories with AI-written captions that match the visuals Arcade: QuizTime Interactive quiz games powered by your library Gameplay recording Auto-record polished gameplay videos of your arcade games Panic mode Instantly hide the app behind a safe screen FAQ Frequently asked questions Bug reports How to report issues

docs.title: Technology stack
docs.text:
• Frontend: React + TypeScript with Tailwind CSS
  • Backend: .NET 10 with Clean Architecture
  • Database: SQLite, bundled with the app
  • Video processing: FFmpeg
  • Downloads: yt-dlp
  • Local AI (optional): Ollama for frame descriptions + embeddings; Python (OpenCV/librosa) for motion & beat analysis

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text: Frequently asked questions about Gero.

docs.title: What is Gero?
docs.text: Gero is a personal media management and streaming platform. It lets you download, organize, tag, and enjoy your video collection through a modern web interface with features like Theater Mode, automatic tagging, media subscriptions, and arcade games. It installs as a native Windows app.

docs.title: Is Gero free?
docs.text:
Gero is available through Patreon. You subscribe to get access to download links. Once downloaded and installed, the app is yours to keep forever — even if you cancel your subscription.

The only thing you lose without an active subscription is access to new updates and features.

docs.title: Is Gero open source?
docs.text: No. Gero is proprietary software. The source code is not publicly available. See the License page for details.

docs.title: What platforms are supported?
docs.text:
Windows — a native app (bundles the API, web UI, SQLite, FFmpeg and yt-dlp). This is the way to run Gero today.

What about Linux / NAS / servers?

There is no Linux, NAS or server version. Gero is a Windows desktop app, and that's the only way to run it.

docs.title: Does my data stay private?
docs.text: Yes. All your data (videos, metadata, settings, accounts) stays on your own hardware. There is no telemetry and no analytics. The only outbound request Gero ever makes is the manual update check, which you have to press a button to start — see our Privacy policy.

docs.title: How do I get Gero?
docs.text:
1. Subscribe on Patreon
  2. Download the Windows build from the supporter portal
  3. Follow the Installation guide

docs.title: Do I need a domain name?
docs.text: No. You can access Gero via IP address (e.g., http://192.168.1.100:9710). A domain is only needed if you want HTTPS or easier remote access.

docs.title: Can I use Gero without internet?
docs.text:
Once installed, Gero runs fully offline. You only need internet for:

  • Downloading videos from online sources
  • Auto-tag extraction from source pages
  • Getting a new version — either downloading it yourself, or pressing Check for updates if you've saved an update key

docs.title: Can I access Gero remotely?
docs.text:
Yes! Options include:

  • Port forwarding on your router
  • Reverse proxy with HTTPS (recommended)
  • VPN or Cloudflare Tunnel

docs.title: What video sources are supported?
docs.text: Any site supported by yt-dlp, which includes thousands of websites. You can also import local video files.

docs.title: What video formats work?
docs.text: Gero supports all formats FFmpeg can process. Videos are automatically converted to browser-compatible formats (MP4/WebM) during import.

docs.title: How does automatic tagging work?
docs.text:
When importing, Gero automatically:

  • Extracts tags from the source page (categories, tags, metadata)
  • Matches tag names and aliases against the video title
  • Links known actors found in the video title
  • Creates thumbnails and animated previews

docs.title: Can I import an existing video library?
docs.text: Yes. You can upload videos through the web UI or drop them into a watched folder.

docs.title: What is Theater Mode?
docs.text:
A full-screen, TikTok/Reels-style player with:

  • Scroll/swipe to navigate between videos
  • Interactive scrubber
  • Keyboard shortcuts (arrow keys, space, M)
  • Mobile-optimized touch gestures

docs.title: Why won't a video play?
docs.text:
Common causes:

  1. Unsupported format — The video needs conversion (re-import it)
  2. Missing file — The video file was deleted from storage
  3. Network issue — Browser can't reach the API
  4. CORS issue — API not configured for your domain

Check the browser console (F12) for specific errors.

docs.title: What do I get with a Patreon subscription?
docs.text: Access to the supporter portal: the Windows build (older versions included), the Android apk, and a personal update key so Gero can fetch new releases for you. The gameplay recordings come with every tier.

docs.title: What happens if I cancel my subscription?
docs.text: Nothing breaks. Your installed version of Gero keeps working indefinitely. You just won't be able to download new versions with features and bug fixes.

docs.title: Is this a one-time purchase?
docs.text: Essentially, yes. Subscribe once, download the app, and it's yours forever. If you want ongoing updates, keep your subscription active.

docs.title: How do I update to a new version?
docs.text:
There are three routes, all covered in the Installation guide:

  1. Manual — download the .zip and copy the files over your existing installation
  2. From a .zip — download the .zip and let Gero install it from Settings → Updates
  3. With an update key — save a key from the supporter downloads page, then press Check for updates and Gero fetches the release itself

docs.title: Does Gero update itself automatically?
docs.text: No. There is no automatic update check of any kind — no schedule, no startup check, no background check. Gero only looks for a newer version when you press Check for updates, and it always shows you the version and release notes and asks for confirmation before downloading anything.

docs.title: Is Gero secure?
docs.text:
Gero includes:

  • Built-in authentication (email + password)
  • Secure password hashing
  • Session management with secure cookies
  • No external data collection

For remote access, we recommend HTTPS via a reverse proxy.

docs.title: Does Gero phone home?
docs.text:
No. Zero telemetry, zero analytics, and nothing running in the background that talks to anyone.

Gero only goes online when you tell it to: when you download content from an online source, and when you press Check for updates. That check goes to your supporter downloads server, carries only the update key you pasted in yourself, and asks one question — is there a newer version? Nothing about your library, your usage or your machine is sent, and without a key the check can't run at all. The full detail is in the Privacy policy.

docs.title: Where are the logs?
docs.text: Check the application window, or the log files in the installation directory.

docs.title: Database migrations failed on startup
docs.text: This is rare. Check the API logs for the specific error. If you're updating from an old version, make sure you're on the latest build.

docs.title: How do I back up my data?
docs.text:
Back up:

  • The database — the SQLite file (in your data/ folder)
  • The storage folder (your media files, thumbnails, previews)

Still have questions? Report a bug or check GitHub Issues.
